title: White bands, the Irish Channel and playing for the Buzzards
summary: White bands at Milneburg; Miller's Buzzards Mardi Gras contract and being threatened walking through the Irish Channel.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What about the white bands? Did they have white bands out there?

Well, they played at Millenburg the most. I mean Spanish food. That's what the most did, they played out that way, see. And we played Millenburg, see. Let me see now. Did you ever play an Irish channel?
Oh yeah, but my God. Did you ever play in the Irish Channel?
Oh yeah, but my God. See, I used to play, I'd sign a contract, I'd finish this Mardi Gras, and sign a contract right there for the next Mardi Gras, for the Buzzards. You ever heard of the Buzzards?

Lord, I used to play for them every year. Buzzards. It was good. I mean, they treat you nice, boy. But in the other way, I remember I could, the only way I got by one time out there, I had to tell them boys who I was and everything. I said, this is Kid Punch. I play for the Buzzards every year. Boy, they're fixing to crucify me. For what? For nothing? They just didn't want you to walk them through that. No business walking through that. That's what that means. Nigga, where you going to walk through? You know where you going? I said, yeah, I live down up here. He said, well, hell, you ain't got no business through here. I said, well, I come to see the man by signing the contract for the Buzzards. I play for the Buzzards every year. So for some reason, this man had a student right across the street, see? And so another boy come up and said, well, there's a man over there. You want to go see him? So I went there. I said, look here. I said, I'm Punch. Kid Punch played for you. He said, oh, yeah, yeah. What's happened? I said, well, I'm trying to get home with the white boy. He's going to whip me up up there. And he come on out of there. I said, god damn, y'all leave that fellow alone. That fellow play music for me every year. Yeah, that's true.
